name: Lynn
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lynn, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Lynn, MA: Festival of Lights in Central Square, the Lynn Common tree lighting, The Nutcracker and the Christmas Eve parade.
lede: Lynn celebrates Christmas with two tree lightings, one in Central Square and one on Lynn Common, a Nutcracker at the city's own auditorium and a Christmas Eve parade that winds through the whole city.
celebrates: The season in Lynn starts downtown. The Greater Lynn Chamber of Commerce, the City of Lynn and Lynn Main Streets hold the Festival of Lights in Central Square, where youth groups dance, the Salvation Army of Lynn pours hot chocolate and the night ends with a tree and menorah lighting. The city then lights its own holiday tree on Lynn Common, with Santa arriving on a fire engine, and opens City Hall for a holiday vendor fair with crafts and cookie decorating. The Greater Salem Ballet Company dances The Nutcracker at the Lynn Memorial Auditorium, and on Christmas Eve, Santa rides through the city in a parade that started in 1986.
lastyear: In 2025 the city's City Hall'iday Festivities began on December 2 with the tree lighting on Lynn Common and a sing-along led by the Lynn Public Schools Chorus, the All-City Marching Band and St. Mary's School, followed by a vendor fair at City Hall with children's crafts, Toe Jam Puppets and photos with Santa. The Festival of Lights came to Central Square on December 8, The Nutcracker played Lynn Auditorium on December 20, and on Christmas Eve Santa and Mrs. Claus waved to crowds on Summer Street and Boston Street during the annual parade.
facts: Lynn's Christmas Eve Parade was started in 1986 by Rich Viger and John's Oil, and after Viger died in 2013 a dedicated committee kept it going. The parade travels about 23 miles through the city, leaving Austin Square at 5 pm on its traditional schedule and sending Santa and Mrs. Claus home to the North Pole around 10 pm. Lynn itself was once called the greatest shoe town in the country, and by the turn of the twentieth century it was the largest shoe-manufacturing city in the world.
trains: Lynn sits on the MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport/Rockport Line, with two stops in the city, River Works and Lynn Interim, and trains running to North Station in Boston. The Eastern Railroad from Boston to Salem passed through Lynn in 1837, which encouraged shoe shops to move from the Lynn Common area toward the tracks. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through Christmas lights, and Lowell has the National Streetcar Museum and the Boston and Maine Railroad Historical Society's steam locomotive No. 410.

traditions: The Greater Lynn Chamber of Commerce lights a holiday tree and a menorah in Central Square after sing-alongs and youth dance performances.
City tree lighting on Lynn Common
Santa rides down Hanover Street on a fire engine to help the City of Lynn light its holiday tree.
Holiday Vendor Fair at City Hall
After the tree lighting, City Hall fills with local makers, cookie decorating, crafts and a glow-in-the-dark dance party.
The Nutcracker at Lynn Memorial Auditorium
The Greater Salem Ballet Company has staged The Nutcracker at the auditorium inside Lynn City Hall for more than a decade.
Richie Viger's People's Parade carries Santa and Mrs. Claus on a route of about 23 miles through Lynn every Christmas Eve.
The Lynn Police Department hosts an annual party where Santa visits and every registered child gets pizza, a cupcake and a holiday gift.
kidfact: On Christmas Eve, Lynn's parade carries Santa and Mrs. Claus on a trip of about 23 miles all over the city before they head back to the North Pole.
faq: When is the Lynn Christmas Eve Parade?

The parade runs every Christmas Eve. On its traditional schedule it leaves Austin Square at 5 pm and winds about 23 miles through Lynn, reaching Lynngate Plaza on Broadway around 9:30 pm. Times along the route are approximate, so follow the Official Lynn MA Christmas Parade Facebook page on the night for updates on where Santa is.
Where are the Christmas tree lightings in Lynn?

Lynn has two. The Festival of Lights lights a holiday tree and a menorah in Central Square in downtown Lynn, hosted by the Greater Lynn Chamber of Commerce with the city and Lynn Main Streets. The City of Lynn also lights its holiday tree on Lynn Common, with Santa arriving on a fire engine, and then opens City Hall for a holiday vendor fair.
Is there a Nutcracker in Lynn?

Yes. The Greater Salem Ballet Company performs The Nutcracker each December at the Lynn Memorial Auditorium inside Lynn City Hall at 3 City Hall Square. The company usually gives two shows on one Saturday, at noon and 4 pm, and sells tickets through the auditorium box office at 781-599-SHOW and lynnauditorium.com.

The City of Lynn says its December holiday events are free and open to the public unless otherwise noted. That covers the city tree lighting and the vendor fair at City Hall, and the Greater Lynn Chamber of Commerce calls the Festival of Lights free and open to all. Ticketed shows at Lynn Auditorium, such as The Nutcracker, are the exception.
How do I get to Lynn by train?

Take the MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport/Rockport Line from North Station in Boston. The line stops twice in Lynn, at River Works and Lynn Interim, before continuing to Swampscott and Salem. The MBTA posts a fall and winter schedule for the line, so check train times before you go.
